claims.text:
Belegorn is a Sindarin name. Its meaning is not glossed, but Paul Strack suggests it means "Great-tree" and is a compound of beleg ("great", "mighty", "large", "big") and orn ([tall] "tree").
Belegorn was probably named after a renowned heroe in the royal lines of old as recorded in legend.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Carl F. Hostetter (ed.), "Part Two. Body, Mind and Spirit: V. Beards", The Nature of Middle-earth, HarperCollins, 2021, footnote 3, p. 189; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", The Ruling Stewards of Gondor, p. 203

claims.text: Belegorn became the fourth Ruling Steward at the death of his father, Steward Herion in .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Realms in Exile", "The Southern Line: Heirs of Anarion", Ruling Stewards, entry for Herion, p. 1039

claims.text: Belegorn's rule was a quiet time for Gondor during the Watchful Peace, when Sauron was in the East and the Nazgûl stayed quiet in Minas Morgul.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "Gondor and the Heirs of Anárion", "The Stewards", fourth paragraph, p. 1053; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age", entries for the years 2063 and 2460, p. 1087

claims.text: Belegorn ruled as Steward for fiftysix years, and was succeeded by his son, Húrin I..
